This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 for setting aside the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30.11.2010 passed by the II Additional District and Special Judge, Dakshina Kannada, Mangalore in Special Case No.6/2006 whereby the trial Court has convicted the accused for the offence punishable under Section 376(1)

4. The case of the prosecution is that as per the complaint filed by one Smt. Seetha [PW.2]-mother of the victim that on 14.01.2006 while herself and her husband went outside the house, her daughter Kumari Asha and her grand father were present in the house.
When they returned to the house in the evening, her daughter was suffering from heavy pain in the veginal part and when enquired there was bleeding injury in her private part.
Immediately she was shifted to Lady Goschen Hospital and from there she was referred to Government Hospital.
There they came to know that the victim girl was sexually assaulted by the accused.

It is stated by the victim girl that when she went to a gujari shop for selling waste materials, the accused came in a scooter and asked her to NC:

After the incident, the victim came near the main road and at that time an auto rickshaw came there and on seeing the condition of the victim, the driver of the auto rickshaw took the victim in the vehicle and dropped her near the house.
A complaint came to be filed as per Ex.P.2.
The police have registered FIR and arrested the accused.

sentences.text: Accordingly, charges were framed by the trial Court.
The accused pleaded not guilty but claimed to be tried.
5. The prosecution to prove its case, in all, examined 24 witnesses as PWs.1 to 24 and 30 documents have been marked as Exs.P.1 to P.30 and 9 objects have been marked as MOs.1 to 9.
After closure of the prosecution witnesses, the NC: 2023:KHC:20907 accused himself examined as DW.1 and got marked Exs.D.1 to D.9.

After hearing the learned counsel for parties, the trial Court having found the guilty of the accused, convicted and sentenced to undergo imprisonment as aforesaid, but the trial Court acquitted him for the offences punishable under Section 3(1)(xi) of the SC/ST (POA) Act.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment of conviction and order of sentence, the appellant is before this Court.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the evidence of the prosecution witnesses are not sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused and there was no seminal stain found in the private part of the victim and there was also no blood stain on the clothes of the victim.
It is contended that there was an error in taking cognizance by the trial Court and once cognizance is taken, the entire trial will be vitiated.
He submitted that as per the evidence of the Doctor, there was no seminal stain in the clothes of the victim [Ex.P3] and the information given by the Doctor is not conclusive.
He submitted that except the testimony of the victim nothing has been elicited from the records.
Hence, he prays for allowing the appeal.

Further the learned counsel contended that all the witnesses, including PWs.4 and 5 and the victim, were all present in the police station and once again they were called to the police station while conducting test identification parade.
Once the witnesses have already identified the accused in the police station, yet again an identification of the accused by the witnesses is not necessary.

PW.5 has stated that he has not at all seen the accused and PW.6 stated that no one was present at the place where the victim was found and evidence of these witnesses are not reliable witnesses to convict the accused.
Hence, he prays to allow the appeal setting aside the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.

8. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader supported the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the trial Court and contended that the evidences of PW.1, victim girl and PW.2, mother of the victim, PW.4 and PW.5 clearly reveal that the accused was taking the T Nagaraja vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166570670/
3 victim girl on his motorbike and when it was stopped near the railway track, they helped the accused by pushing the motorbike and thereafter, he took the victim girl on his NC: 2023:KHC:20907 motorbike.

sentences.text: The evidence of PWs.4 and 5 corroborates the evidence of PW.2, the complainant.
The evidence of PW.8 who treated the victim girl clearly reveals that there was bleeding in the veginal part of the victim girl.
Except denial and formal suggestions, nothing has been elicited from the evidence of PW.8-Doctor who actually examined the victim, found injuries and given the opinion.

The evidence of PWs.1, 2, 3, 4 , 5, 6 and 8 and evidence of Doctor and Investigating Officer clearly establish the offences committed by the accused and there is no error in the judgment of conviction and order of sentence which does not call for interference.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

9. Having heard the learned counsels for the parties, the point that arises for consideration by this Court are:
"(i) Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt, that on 14.01.2006 at about 11.00 a.m., the accused assured the victim girl on the ground that he would pay Rs.100/- to clean the house, took her on his scooter, threatened her with dire consequences and committed forcible sexual intercourse thereby he committed the offences under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC.
NC: 2023:KHC:20907 (ii) The judgment and conviction calls for any interference by this Court?"

10. Upon hearing the contention of the learned counsel, on perusal of the records and in order to re-appreciate the evidence on record, it is necessary to have a cursory look into the evidence adduced by the prosecution before the Trial Court which are as under:
(a) PW.1-the victim girl aged about 9 years has deposed before the trial Court on oath that in the year 2006 she was studying in 2nd standard and on 14.01.2006 there was holiday for the school on the eve of 'Sankranthi Festival' and when her parents went outside the house, she went to the scrap shop for selling scrapes and obtained Rs.20/-.

On the way the accused came there and assured her to pay Rs.100/-
for cleaning the house.

Believing the version of the accused, the victim girl accompanied him in the scooter and when they reached near the railway station, it was stopped and there two persons were standing near the railway track and the accused called them to help him and they pushed the scooter and later accused took her to home and by threatening with dire consequences, made her to lay on the ground and removed her NC: 2023:KHC:20907 clothes and committed sexual intercourse on her.
The accused also has beaten her chest due to which she has heavy pain and due to forcible intercourse there was bleeding in veginal part.

After this incident, she worn her dresses and came out of the house and when she was standing near the bus stop, an auto- rickshaw came there and on seeing her, driver of the auto rickshaw took her and dropped near the house.
She narrated the incident to her mother PW.2.

This witness has also stated that earlier she went to Lady Goschen hospital where the victim girl narrated the incident to her and from there went to Government hospital.
The evidence of this witness cannot be discarded to disbelieve the case of the prosecution.
Though this witness is not an eyewitness to the incident and she received the information from the victim minor daughter of nine years, she lodged the complaint before the police.
Therefore, the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 corroborates each other.
(c) PW.3-Mallesha, the father of the victim and husband of PW.2 who also came to know about the incident when he came to the house through PWs.1 and 2.
He also deposes that he accompanied with the wife and daughter to the hospital and while lodging the complaint.

- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 (d) PWs.4 and 5-Rajesh and Deepak are the chance witnesses where the accused while taking the victim girl-PW.1 in his scooter, the scooter was stopped near the Railway gate, at that time, the accused requested them to push the said scooter, then these two witnesses pushed the scooter and then the scooter was started and accused went away.
These two witnesses have stated at the time of pushing the scooter, the victim girl was a pillion rider of the scooter.

PW.5 is the known person to the accused and PW.4 was known to PW.5, both of them stood near the railway crossing, they seen the accused taking the victim in his scooter and later, they came to know that the accused committed sexual assault on the victim girl and thereafter, they both went to the Police Station and seen the accused in the Police Station and these two witnesses further deposes that later the Tahsildar summoned them where once again they identified the accused, the accused was made to stand in the row.

The evidence of PW.6 who is - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 the circumstantial evidence took the victim girl from the place of incident has not been challenged by the learned counsel for the accused.
(f) PW.7-Dr.K.Mohandas Bhandary deposes that on 14.01.2006 at 3.30 p.m., PW.1 was brought by her parents on the history of rape, then, he has referred them to the Government Hospital.
He also given statement before the Police.
His evidence is also not disputed by the learned counsel for the accused.
(g) PW.8-Dr.Jacintha D'Souza, doctor from Wenlock Hospital, Mangaluru also deposed that on 14.01.2006 at 4.30 p.m., the victim was brought to the hospital with the history of sexual assault.
He has examined the victim girl and also recorded the case history.
The victim has stated that the accused took her to the house and committed rape on her.
Thereafter, PW.8 verified there was injuries found on the private part, the hymen was torn and the victim was suffering lot of pain in her veginal part.
He found 3 x 4 cm of torn injury on the private part, also found almost 8 injuries on the body and even he found injuries on the chest.
Then, he has - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 collected cloth of the victim for the purpose of chemical analysis and also collected the vaginal swab and sent for the chemical analysis.
He was given opinion that as per Ex.P.3, there was sexual assault on the victim girl.

During the cross examination, except denial and formal suggestions, nothing has been elicited by the learned counsel for the accused to disbelieve the evidence of PW.8-Doctor who actually examined the victim, found injuries and given the opinion.
(h) PW.9-Jayananda Poojary, Junior Engineer, P.W.D., who prepared the spot sketch as per Ex.P.10 as per the instruction of the Police.
He is only a formal witness.

(j) PW.10-K.B.Ramachandra, Tahsildar, who conducted the Test Identification Parade (TIP) in the jail where PWs.1, 4 and 5 were identified the accused and issued the report as per Exs.P.9 and 10 and he also prepared the panchanama as per Ex.P.11.
Of course, this witness conducted the TIP where the victim as well as PWs.4 and 5 identified the accused as he is the assailant.

However, it is brought to the notice of this Court by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant where the evidence of the witness i.e., PWs.1, 4 and 5 clearly reveals - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 prior to conducting the TIP, these witnesses were seen the accused in the Police Station.

Though as per Section 9 of the Evidence Act, the identity of the accused during the T Nagaraja vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166570670/
6 TIP is relevant fact to be proved by the prosecution, but, here in this case, the witnesses seen the accused in the Police Station prior to conducting the TIP.

sentences.text: Therefore, though the evidence of identification of the accused by the witnesses as per PWs.1, 4 and 5, but in view of the accused seen by these witnesses in the Police Station and subsequent to the identity of the accused in the prison is not acceptable and therefore, accepting the report of TIP is not correct.

However, it is well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the witnesses and circumstances were able to prove the case of the accused even without TIP, the Court can proceed to convict the accused.
Therefore, the evidence of the witnesses by PW.10 is having no much reliance and helpful to the prosecution case.

(k) PW.11-Sheikh Hassan Saheb, Revenue Inspector who issued the document in respect of spot i.e.,
house of the accused who is the formal witness.

This evidence is also not disputed.
(n) PW.14-Raja, panch witness as per Ex.P.19 (p) PW.15-Rajkumar who is also a panch witness to Ex.P.19 where the victim shown the spot and they conducted the panchanama.
(q) PW.16-Nagappa is also a panch witness to Ex.P.1- spot panch and this witness also turned hostile.
(r) PW.17-Narayana Poojary, another panch witness to the panchanama and also for seizure of the scooter turned hostile.
(s) PW.18-Chand Saheb, Tahsildar who issued the caste certified as per Ex.P.23.

Since the trial Court has already acquitted the appellant for the offence under the SC/ST (POA) Act and there was no appeal by the State and when accused taken the victim with him, he was not aware about the caste of - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 the victim.
Therefore, attracting Section 3(1) of the SC/ST (POA) Act is not correct and the Trial Court has rightly acquitted the appellant under the SC/ST (POA) Act.

11. On perusal of the entire evidence on record, the evidence of PW.1-the victim girl aged about 9 years has clearly stated about the incident where the accused took her in his - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 scooter on 14.01.2006 and committed sexual assault on her in the house.
The evidence of PW.1 clearly corroborate with the evidence of PW.2 who came to know about the incident from the daughter and she lodged the complaint to the Police.
To corroborate the evidence of PW.1, the evidence of PWs.4 and 5 are the circumstantial witnesses have seen the company of the victim with the accused in the scooter of the accused on the said day.
The evidence of PW.6 who was the auto driver is that immediately after the incident, he took the victim and dropped near the house.
The evidence of PW.7-Dr.Mohandas Bhandary have examined the victim at the first instance and after coming to know about the medico legal case, he referred the victim to the Government Hospital and

PW.8-The doctor who examined the victim girl has clinically found various injures on the private part and on the body of the victim and given certificate and opinion that she was subjected to the rape.
The evidence of PWs.1, 2, 4 to 8 also corroborates with the evidence of the Investigating Officer who conducted the investigation and filed the charge sheet.

With regard to the identity of the accused, the victim went along with the accused, traveled with him to the house,
where the accused committed sexual assault by - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 threatening her and sent her out of the house.
Thereafter, she came home and informed and she also identified the accused in the Police Station.
PW.5, who is the known person to the accused has pushed the scooter along with PW.4.

Though the accused examined DW.1 one Vasantha Kumar who said to be the driver of the lorry has stated that PW.4 is the person behind the incident have falsely implicating the accused in the crime that merely the accused contested the T Nagaraja vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166570670/
8 Mahanagara Palike elections and defeated in the election.

sentences.text: That itself cannot be a ground for implicating the accused falsely, that too in a rape case where the victim aged about nine years and her parents would support PW.4 for falsely implicating the accused.
If at all, if it is a false implication, there could not be any injuries on the private part and chest of the victim which was examined on the very same day.
Therefore, the defence taken by the accused that the false implication by PW.4 in the criminal case is not acceptable.

12. On perusal of the entire evidence on record, the evidence of the prosecution witnesses i.e.,
PWs.1, 2 and 4 to 8 and PWs.23 and 24, I am of the view, the prosecution established the fact of commission of rape and also threatened - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 the victim by the accused.
Thereby, he has committed the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC beyond all reasonable doubt.
As regards to the findings of the Trial Court, the Trial Court by relying upon the evidence had given reasons which is sufficient for accepting by this Court in the jurisdiction.
Absolutely, there is no error committed by the trial Court in respect of finding guilt of the accused in the above said offences.

13. Though the prosecution also filed the charge sheet under Section 3(1) of the SC/ST (POA) Act and certificate issued regarding caste by the Tahsildar, but at the time of incident, the accused was not aware that she belong to the SC/ST community and thereby, he has committed rape.

Therefore,
the trial Court has rightly acquitted the accused under SC/ST (POA) Act and though, the learned counsel for the appellant has contended that for taking cognizance, there is no application of mind by the trial Court, just it was relied upon the police statement, thereby the trial vitiates.
But looking to the order sheet, though the trial Court has stated that there is a case made out by the prosecution for proceeding and taking cognizance.

This Court in the case of Sri Abbas Mohammed - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 Khan vs. The Deputy Director and Another in W.P.No.14245/2021 dated 25.01.2022 has taken a view that when the Police filed the challan and the Investigating Officer given opinion, the Magistrate need not give any detailed reason for taking cognizance as required in the case where the private complaint filed by the complainant under Section 2(d) read with Section 200 of Cr.P.C. and to record the sworn statement where the Magistrate required to apply his mind for taking cognizance and proceed with the case and issuing process under Section 204 of Cr.P.C.
Therefore, I am of the view, there is no error committed by the Trial Court in taking cognizance by mentioning the charge-sheet filed by the Investigating Officer.

entities.text: Sri Abbas Mohammed - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 Khan vs. The Deputy Director and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, on that ground, I am of the view, the trial cannot be vitiated and if any error in framing of charge, that can be curable defect as per Section 465 of Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, the contention of learned counsel cannot be acceptable.

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
The appeal is dismissed.

Therefore, though the evidence of identification of the accused by the witnesses as per PWs.1, 4 and 5, but in view of the accused seen by these witnesses in the Police Station and subsequent to the identity of the accused in the prison is not acceptable and therefore, accepting the report of TIP is not correct.
However, it is well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the witnesses and circumstances were able to prove the case of the accused even without TIP, the Court can proceed to convict the accused.
Since the trial Court has already acquitted the appellant for the offence under the SC/ST (POA) Act and there was no appeal by the State and when accused taken the victim with him, he was not aware about the caste of - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:20907 the victim.
Therefore, attracting Section 3(1) of the SC/ST (POA) Act is not correct and the Trial Court has rightly acquitted the appellant under the SC/ST (POA) Act.
That itself cannot be a ground for implicating the accused falsely, that too in a rape case where the victim aged about nine years and her parents would support PW.4 for falsely implicating the accused.
If at all, if it is a false implication, there could not be any injuries on the private part and chest of the victim which was examined on the very same day.
Therefore, the defence taken by the accused that the false implication by PW.4 in the criminal case is not acceptable.
Thereby, he has committed the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC beyond all reasonable doubt.
As regards to the findings of the Trial Court, the Trial Court by relying upon the evidence had given reasons which is sufficient for accepting by this Court in the jurisdiction.
Absolutely, there is no error committed by the trial Court in respect of finding guilt of the accused in the above said offences.
13. Though the prosecution also filed the charge sheet under Section 3(1) of the SC/ST (POA) Act and certificate issued regarding caste by the Tahsildar, but at the time of incident, the accused was not aware that she belong to the SC/ST community and thereby, he has committed rape.
Therefore,
the trial Court has rightly acquitted the accused under SC/ST (POA) Act and though, the learned counsel for the appellant has contended that for taking cognizance, there is no application of mind by the trial Court, just it was relied upon the police statement, thereby the trial vitiates.
Therefore, on that ground, I am of the view, the trial cannot be vitiated and if any error in framing of charge, that can be curable defect as per Section 465 of Cr.P.C.
